messages:
Ava: heads-up — noticed a regression in streaming chunk cadence after the kernel-selector rollout this morning :eyes:
Ava: p50 token-latency for small chat requests jumped from 12ms -> 22ms, p95 from 48ms -> 110ms. dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/streams/stream-cadence?id=stream-cadence
Ravi: can you paste the per-token waterfall? need to see client vs server timing (are we batching more or flushing less?)
Ava: snippet from profiler (nvtx + runtime trace):
```
[server] token_emit: 8ms
[kernel_select] overhead: 9-12ms when switching to fallback kernel
batcher_wait: 4-6ms depending on batcher window
network_send: 1-2ms
```
Ava: interestingly the KV cache hit ratio is flat, but KV lookup latency sometimes spikes ~10ms for cold keys
Jo: on the frontend I see chunk boundaries arriving less frequently, clients show bigger gaps between chunks (client-side timestamps line up with server flush times)
Kai: we rolled kernel-selector v2 at 06:12 UTC, it prefers optimized kernels but falls back for long sequences. Could fallback path be slower due to memcpy patterns?
perf-bot: perf-regression alert: service=streaming-api, commit=6a3f2d1, p95_token_latency:+130% over baseline, linked traces: https://perf.redwood.ai/trace/6a3f2d1
Ravi: does the runtime emit a token-level breakdown metric? we need token_emit_server_ms vs token_receive_client_ms per chunk to separate network vs compute
Ava: not right now — we have total token latency and a coarse breakdown (compute vs net) but not per-chunk. I can add a small span in the stream flush path to tag stream_chunk_flush_server_ts
Jo: also check client-side flush cadence: we've changed our chunk size heuristic last month (bigger chunks) — but the regression correlates with the kernel change timing
Kai: quick repro idea: run stream load test with env var KERNEL_SELECTOR_DEBUG=1 and KV_TTL=0 to force cold KV; capture timeline with --emit-timestamps
Ava: ran local repro with ~50 concurrent streams, attached excerpt:
```
[trace id=abc123]
0.000 request_start
0.018 first_token_server_emit
0.048 token_42_kernel_switch
0.080 token_42_emit
0.220 token_43_emit (fallback kernel)

observed: fallback kernel adds ~140ms on long tails per affected token
```
Ravi: who owns the kernel selector micro-optimizations? ping @Kai to convo about memcpy and CUDA kernel launch overheads
Kai: will investigate memcpy paths and whether we added sync points. also will check kernel cache warmup heuristics — maybe the selector is evicting optimized kernels too aggressively
Ava: next steps I propose:
- instrument token-level server vs client timestamps (short-term flag)
- add per-route KPI in console: p50/p95 token_emit_ms, chunk_cadence_ms, stream_stall_count
- run an A/B rollback of kernel-selector v2 for 1 hour on a subset (canary)
- reproduce with KV cold hits to ensure not a cache interplay
Ravi: agreed. I'll add dashboards and a lightweight trace aggregator that builds token waterfalls per request id
Jo: I'll add client-side timing logs for a small % of users and correlate via request id
perf-bot: action created: PERF-3247 (investigate streaming token p95 regression) — assignees: Ava, Kai, Ravi
Ava: thanks — I'll open the trace PR and toggle flag behind runtime.feature.streaming_token_spans. will post results here once we have numbers :thumbsup:
Kai: starting kernel selector audit now, will report findings by EOD
Jo: keeping a watch on client logs, will post samples if we see mismatched timestamps
Ravi: tagging ops to hold a rollback window if needed: @ops-team :bell:
Ava: OK, closing thread for now — will update when we have the new token spans and can compare server vs client waterfalls
